slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will make you
impossible to manipulate

reading the small print

read the full terms of one thing you sign up for this month. learning how companies hide the important parts trains you to spot when people try the very same thing.

sleeping on decisions

never say yes to anything important on the day it's offered. pressure to decide right now is the oldest trick there is, and one night of sleep beats it almost every time.

studying ads

pick one advert a day and ask yourself what feeling it's trying to sell you. once you see the trick in adverts, you start seeing exactly the same trick in people.

how the mind works

spend 5 minutes a day learning one idea from psychology: anchoring, social proof, the scarcity trap. you can't be fooled by a trick you already know the name of.

slides.texte_overlay:
asking why twice

when someone wants something from you, ask yourself why they want it, then ask why again. the second answer is usually the real one, and it's rarely the one they gave you.
